explanation.question_quote: The patient reports being quite active and able to climb 3 flights of stairs in his building 10 years ago, whereas now he feels extremely winded when climbing a single flight. At first, he attributed this to old age but has more recently begun noticing that he feels similarly short of breath when lying down.
explanation.sentence: He has progressive exertional dyspnea and now becomes short of breath when lying flat.
Orthopnea, bibasilar crackles, a palpable liver edge, and bilateral leg edema together point to heart failure with pulmonary and systemic congestion.

explanation.question_quote: A cardiac catheterization report from 5 years ago reveals a moderately enlarged heart but patent coronary arteries.
explanation.sentence: His prior catheterization showed cardiac enlargement despite patent coronary arteries.
Nightly drinking and prior hospitalizations for “the shakes,” suggestive of alcohol withdrawal, make alcohol-induced toxic cardiomyopathy the most likely cause of his heart failure.
Cardiac enlargement favors a dilated cardiomyopathy over isolated diastolic heart failure, although an echocardiogram is needed to assess ventricular function.
